subject.title: Grossmont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 5

text: As a dedicated leader for the Grossmont Union High School District, I prioritize academic excellence over politics. I’m honored to be endorsed by Congressman Darrell Issa, San Diego County Supervisor Joel Anderson, State Senator Brian Jones, El Cajon Mayor Bill Wells, and current and former board members Gary Woods, Evelyn Wills, Gary Cass, and retired West Hills High School teacher Ralph Hayes.

Under my leadership, we have modernized facilities, increased teacher pay, improved student safety, and protected taxpayer funds. I am committed to enhancing funding for sports, arts, and extracurricular activities, ensuring a well-rounded education for all students.

With 33 years of experience representing San Diego East County families—10 years on the San Diego County Board of Education and 23 years on the Grossmont Union High School Board—I hold a bachelor’s degree in business administration from Cal Poly San Luis Obispo and a master’s degree in education from San Diego State University. My wife, Mary Kelly, a retired public-school teacher, and I are proud parents of three sons and seven grandsons.

text: As a 36-year West Hills High School educator with lifelong ties to East County, I know what is at stake. I’ve seen firsthand how poor decisions and a lack of transparency ripple through our classrooms, affecting students, teachers, staff and families.
I care deeply about this community because it has given so much to my family. That’s why I’m running for the Grossmont Union High School District Board.
East County is my home. I graduated from El Capitan High School, and so did my children. My wife and I are active in Lakeside Christian Church.
I will refresh the trust lost by many families, employees, and taxpayers, along with restoring fiscal responsibility.
Our community deserves better than public money payouts for lawsuit settlements, closed door meeting violations, grand jury investigations and Public Employee Relations Board investigations.

It’s time to turn the page. As a recently retired teacher, I’ll restore trust, protect taxpayer dollars, and get GUHSD back to doing what it should have been doing all along: helping all of our students succeed
